none: Only من أي شيء coincides; this report concerns the minbar's material and prayer posture, not human creation.

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: At a funeral, the Prophet says each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written; when asked whether to rely on that, he commands action, since each is made easy, citing the giving verse.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَلِيٍّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: At a funeral, the Prophet says each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written; when asked whether to rely on that, he commands action, since each is made easy, citing the giving verse.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَلِيٍّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي جِنَازَةٍ فَأَخَذَ عُودًا فَجَعَلَ

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports true dreams and worship in Hira before Gabriel pressed Muhammad three times, met his 'I cannot read,' then recited the opening revelation through 96:5; Muhammad returned trembling, and revelation later paused after Waraqa died.
rows.anchor: أن عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت كان أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report glosses the Prophet's tahannuth in Hira as worship.
rows.anchor: فيتحنث فيه قال والتحنث التعبد الليالي

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Khadija reassures Muhammad that God will not disgrace him, citing his care for kin, honesty, service to the needy, hospitality, and help in righteous crises.
rows.anchor: قَالَتْ خَدِيجَةُ كَلاَّ أَبْشِرْ، فَوَاللَّهِ لاَ يُخْزِيكَ اللَّهُ أَبَدًا، فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرَّحِمَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative identifies Waraqa as Khadija's cousin, a pre-Islamic Christian who wrote Arabic and Gospel passages in Arabic; he was elderly and blind.
rows.anchor: وَرَقَةَ بْنِ نَوْفَلٍ وَهْوَ ابْنُ عَمِّ خَدِيجَةَ أَخِي أَبِيهَا، وَكَانَ امْرَأً تَنَصَّرَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ

rows.speaker: ورقة
rows.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the namus sent to Moses and wishes he were young and alive to help Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ هَذَا النَّامُوسُ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى مُوسَى، لَيْتَنِي فِيهَا جَذَعًا، لَيْتَنِي أَكُونُ حَيًّا

rows.speaker: ورقة
rows.claim: Waraqa says that anyone bringing such a message is harmed and promises Muhammad strong support if he lives to see that day.
rows.anchor: قَالَ وَرَقَةُ نَعَمْ لَمْ يَأْتِ رَجُلٌ بِمَا جِئْتَ بِهِ إِلاَّ أُوذِيَ، وَإِنْ يُدْرِكْنِي يَوْمُكَ حَيًّا أَنْصُرَكَ نَصْرًا مُؤَزَّرًا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports true dreams preceding worship in Hira, then Gabriel's three embraces and recitation of the opening verses through 96:5; Muhammad returned trembling, asked to be covered, and feared for himself.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ أَوَّلُ مَا بُدِئَ بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ الْوَحْىِ الرُّؤْيَا الصَّادِقَةُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report glosses the Prophet's tahannuth in Hira as worship.
rows.anchor: فيتحنث فيه وهو التعبد الليالي ذوات العدد

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Khadija comforts Muhammad, assuring him God will not disgrace him because he maintains kinship, tells the truth, bears burdens, feeds guests, and helps in right causes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative identifies Waraqa as Khadija's cousin, a pre-Islamic Christian who wrote Arabic and Gospel passages in Arabic; he was elderly and blind.
rows.anchor: وَرَقَةَ بْنِ نَوْفَلِ بْنِ أَسَدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْعُزَّى بْنِ قُصَىٍّ ـ وَهُوَ ابْنُ عَمِّ خَدِيجَةَ أَخُو أَبِيهَا، وَكَانَ امْرَأً تَنَصَّرَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ

rows.speaker: ورقة
rows.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the messenger sent to Moses and wishes he could live until Muhammad's people expel him.
rows.anchor: فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ هَذَا النَّامُوسُ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى مُوسَى، يَا لَيْتَنِي فِيهَا جَذَعًا أَكُونُ حَيًّا، حِينَ يُخْرِجُكَ قَوْمُكَ

rows.speaker: ورقة
rows.claim: Waraqa says anyone bringing this message will face opposition and pledges to support Muhammad if he lives to see the day.
rows.anchor: فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ نَعَمْ، لَمْ يَأْتِ رَجُلٌ قَطُّ بِمَا جِئْتَ بِهِ إِلاَّ عُودِيَ، وَإِنْ يُدْرِكْنِي يَوْمُكَ أَنْصُرَكَ نَصْرًا مُؤَزَّرًا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an account introduced as what reached them, Muhammad repeatedly considered throwing himself from mountain summits during the pause; Gabriel affirmed his prophethood and calmed him.
rows.anchor: فِيمَا بَلَغَنَا حُزْنًا غَدَا مِنْهُ مِرَارًا كَىْ يَتَرَدَّى مِنْ رُءُوسِ شَوَاهِقِ الْجِبَالِ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the cleaver of daybreak as the sun's light by day and the moon's light by night.
rows.anchor: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ ‏{‏فَالِقُ الإِصْبَاحِ‏}‏ ضَوْءُ الشَّمْسِ بِالنَّهَارِ، وَضَوْءُ الْقَمَرِ بِاللَّيْلِ

rows.speaker: أسامة
rows.claim: When urged to approach an official, Usama says he counsels him privately to avoid opening a public controversy and refuses to call a ruler the best after hearing the Prophet's warning.
rows.anchor: قِيلَ لأُسَامَةَ لَوْ أَتَيْتَ فُلاَنًا فَكَلَّمْتَهُ‏.‏ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَرَوْنَ أَنِّي لاَ أُكَلِّمُهُ إِلاَّ أُسْمِعُكُمْ

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that a man who commands right and forbids wrong while doing the opposite will suffer in Hell, his entrails spilling as he circles like a donkey at a mill.
rows.anchor: مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
